title: High as the Heavens Above the Ground
description: High as the Heavens Above the Ground in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 115, headed “God the avenger of his saints; or, His kingdom”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: High as the heavens a-bove the ground Reigns the Cre-a-tor God; Wide as the whole cre-a-tion's bound Ex-tends his aw-ful rod.

lines: High as the heavens above the ground
Reigns the Creator God;
Wide as the whole creation's bound
Extends his awful rod.
Let princes of exalted state
To him ascribe their crown,
Render their homage at his feet,
And cast their glories down.
Know that his kingdom is supreme,
Your lofty thoughts are vain;
He calls you gods, that awful name,
But ye must die like men.
Then let the sovereigns of the globe
Not dare to vex the just;
He puts on vengeance like a robe,
And treads the worms to dust.
Ye judges of the earth, be wise,
And think on heaven with fear;
The meanest saint that you despise
Has an avenger there.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
